diff.interpretation: same_letter_rate near 0 means the chosen revision stayed the same while the letter flipped, i.e. content-driven answers; near 1 means the same letter was chosen in both orders, i.e. position-following; near 0.5 is consistent with a random letter choice. Accuracy must be read alongside this rate, because a stable but wrong semantic choice also produces a rate near 0.

ctrl.interpretation: same_letter_rate near 0 means the chosen revision stayed the same while the letter flipped, i.e. content-driven answers; near 1 means the same letter was chosen in both orders, i.e. position-following; near 0.5 is consistent with a random letter choice. Accuracy must be read alongside this rate, because a stable but wrong semantic choice also produces a rate near 0.

open.interpretation: same_letter_rate near 0 means the chosen revision stayed the same while the letter flipped, i.e. content-driven answers; near 1 means the same letter was chosen in both orders, i.e. position-following; near 0.5 is consistent with a random letter choice. Accuracy must be read alongside this rate, because a stable but wrong semantic choice also produces a rate near 0.

stable.definition: both orders correct; position-insensitive primary endpoint

change_subset_reference.definition: Pairs split by whether the diff_fwd change list contains a security_relevant=true item. The split is selected by the model's own change list, so it is descriptive; open/ctrl are evaluated on the same pairs as a reference, not as a randomized control.

examples.definition: Deterministic examples from the forward order; chosen by decision/correctness pattern, not by hand.

semantic_changes: In the non-verbose MESSAGE_UPDATE branch, the length check before accessing message[3] changed from len < 1 to len < 10, so the truncated-message guard now requires a longer TLV before reading message[3].
diff_only_correct.rationale: In VERSION_A the non-verbose MESSAGE_UPDATE path only checks len < 1 before reading message[3], but message[3] is at offset 3 within the TLV, so a TLV with len 1 or 2 causes an out-of-bounds read. VERSION_B's len < 10 check ensures message[3] is within the TLV before accessing it.

semantic_changes: Replaced assertx(salt) with a null check in the condition (salt && salt[0] == '\0'), so a null salt no longer triggers an assertion but is passed through to string_crypt.
diff_only_correct.rationale: Version A asserts salt is non-null before dereferencing and passing it on, enforcing the API contract. Version B silently accepts a null salt and forwards it to string_crypt, which may dereference it (null-pointer crash) or behave unexpectedly; the null check only guards the notice, not the crypt call.

semantic_changes: In the SIOCGIFADDR case, the copy_to_user failure path now breaks out before calling ipxitf_put(ipxif), whereas previously ipxitf_put was always called after copy_to_user regardless of failure. This introduces a reference leak on copy_to_us
diff_only_correct.rationale: Version B skips ipxitf_put(ipxif) when copy_to_user fails, leaking the ipx_interface reference (and its net_device reference) on each failed SIOCGIFADDR call, which can be triggered repeatedly by an unprivileged user to exhaust resources. Version A always releases the reference.

semantic_changes: On list allocation failure, VERSION_A calls try_free_empty_list on each list, while VERSION_B calls rz_list_free on each list.
ctrl_only_correct.rationale: Both revisions free the lists on allocation failure but then continue to use ret and its (now freed or NULL) lists via _luac_build_info and luac_add_entry, and return ret; neither returns NULL or aborts after the failure branch, so a use-after-free/NULL-deref path remains in both. semantic_changes: zsocket_bind call changed from passing the description directly as the endpoint to passing it as a printf-style format argument with "%s".
zsocket_connect call changed from passing the description directly as the endpoint to passing it as a printf-style format argument with "%s".
ctrl_only_correct.rationale: In czmq, zsocket_bind/zsocket_connect are variadic printf-style functions that format the endpoint from the format string. Version B passes "%s" as the format and the description as an argument, so the endpoint becomes the literal string "%s" rather than the configured address; this breaks the intended bind/connect tar

semantic_changes: The method called on each agent host changed from ForceDetachAllSessions() to ForceDetachAllClients().
ctrl_only_correct.rationale: The only change is which detach method is invoked on each agent host. Both revisions iterate over a copy of the map and force-detach sessions/clients; neither introduces an obvious memory-safety or security flaw in this function itself. The difference is a behavioral/API naming change, not a demonstrable vulnerability.

diff_neither_ctrl_ab.rationale: The change only broadens when flush command control is allocated; it does not introduce an obvious memory-safety or privilege issue, and both revisions otherwise handle allocation and error paths identically. No clear vulnerability is present in either revision.

semantic_changes: Removed a stray duplicate function signature line that was accidentally pasted into the function body.

diff_ab_ctrl_neither.rationale: Version A contains a stray nested function declaration inside the body and passes a TabContents* where a WebContents* is expected, which would fail to compile or, if coerced, pass an invalid pointer; Version B correctly extracts web_contents().

semantic_changes: The reserved-name check now also rejects names that are shadow table names when read-only shadow tables are enabled, via an added OR condition calling sqlite3ReadOnlyShadowTables() and sqlite3ShadowTableName().
